citations.quote: Aligning with the standards for traditional financial services, the new regimes will bolster investor protection.

summary: On 26 May 2026, the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) published conclusions to their joint consultation on proposed licensing regimes for virtual asset advisory and virtual asset management services. The consultation drew 51 responses, described as showing broad market support. The new regimes' scope will align with the SFC's existing Type 4 (advising on securities) and Type 9 (asset management) regulated-activity categories. This follows the already-concluded consultations on virtual asset dealing and custodian regimes; FSTB and SFC will now finalise the advisory and management regimes' legislative proposals as amendments to the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance, targeting introduction of a bill to the Legislative Council within 2026.
title: FSTB and SFC conclude consultations on virtual asset advisory and management regimes
why_it_matters: For a newcomer, this confirms that Hong Kong's two remaining planned virtual-asset licensing gaps -- advisory and asset-management services -- will be regulated using the same activity categories as existing securities advisers and asset managers. Together with the already-concluded virtual asset dealing and custodian regimes, this completes consultation on all four planned virtual-asset licensing regimes (dealing, custodian, advisory, and management), with FSTB and SFC now targeting introduction of a bill to the Legislative Council within 2026 covering the advisory and management regimes.
